eyebrow: T-SQL for Database Administrators · Chapter Five
subtitle: Lesson 23 · Backup & Recovery with T-SQL

code:
SELECT
    d.name AS database_name,
    MAX(CASE WHEN b.type = 'D' THEN b.backup_finish_date END) AS last_full,
    MAX(CASE WHEN b.type = 'I' THEN b.backup_finish_date END) AS last_diff,
    MAX(CASE WHEN b.type = 'L' THEN b.backup_finish_date END) AS last_log
FROM sys.databases d
LEFT JOIN msdb.dbo.backupset b ON b.database_name = d.name
WHERE d.name NOT IN ('tempdb')
GROUP BY d.name
ORDER BY last_full DESC;
caption: A NULL last_full means that database has never been backed up.

eyebrow: Which physical file did it land in?
code:
SELECT
    b.database_name,
    b.backup_start_date,
    m.physical_device_name
FROM msdb.dbo.backupset b
JOIN msdb.dbo.backupmediafamily m
    ON b.media_set_id = m.media_set_id
WHERE b.database_name = 'AdventureWorks2012'
ORDER BY b.backup_start_date DESC;
caption: Essential when backups rotate across files or a network share.
